basis: main was RED. On a clean clone, bash scripts/dirty-path-guard.sh --self-test exited 1 with 35 ok and 1 FAIL: 'a caller passes more than 1 argument(s) to --check-commit', naming scripts/merge-in-gate.sh:125, which read `scripts/dirty-path-guard.sh --check-commit that the CI file`. The line is a wrapped English sentence in merge-in-gate.sh's --explain documentation block, but the matcher's old rule -- 'a tracked line whose first word is this script (optionally preceded by bash/sh), followed by --check-commit' -- allowed ANY leading indentation, so it read the sentence as a command and counted 'that the CI file' as four arguments. The ARITY rule was never wrong; the definition of COMMAND POSITION was too loose. This is the same cries-wolf species as the AFC-241 finding, in the other direction: the guard's own header says a control that cries wolf gets muted. Two changes, and neither weakens the arity check. (1) DOCUMENTATION, scripts/merge-in-gate.sh: the --explain block now reads '... and asks, via scripts/dirty-path-guard.sh, the SAME --check-commit the CI file asks.' Neither the script path nor the flag begins a line in command position; the sentence says the same thing it said before. (2) MATCHER, scripts/dirty-path-guard.sh _audit_callers(): command position is now three unambiguous shapes -- a bash/sh(/bin/...)-prefixed line at any indentation, a column-0 line, and a tab-indented Makefile recipe -- all of which are audited with ANY argument list, bare words included. A token that names the script but is introduced by SPACES ALONE is a wrapped prose continuation, not a command, UNLESS its argument list carries shell evidence (a quote or a variable reference), which every real revision argument has and a sentence does not. This is a PRECISION fix, not a loosening: the shapes a real caller actually takes (bash/sh prefix, tab recipe) are unchanged, and the dispatcher still refuses a surplus argument at the boundary in both modes (assertion 11i, unchanged). The ONLY shape that stops being pre-flight audited is a space-indented BARE invocation with no shell evidence, and it is now named in the header's NOT-audited list; the dispatcher catches a real caller of that shape when it runs, just not before. (3) REGRESSION ASSERTION 11j: a SEPARATE probe repository (for the reason 11g gives -- each probe must hold only the shape it tests) plants the exact class, a space-indented wrapped sentence beginning with the script path and the flag, and asserts it is NOT a caller and is NOT counted, WHILE two genuine one-argument callers beside it still count; then it plants a space-indented bare caller WITH shell evidence and TWO arguments and asserts that it IS still caught. Both directions, so neither a blanket refusal of space-indented lines nor a loosened scan can pass it. ASSERTION COUNT 36 -> 38 (11j adds one echo pair; the matcher change adds no assertion of its own). VERIFIED, on the working tree and independently: --self-test exit 0, 38 ok, 0 FAIL; the same command at the parent revision aecf003 exits 1 with the single FAIL; merge-in-gate.sh --self-test exit 0; --explain prints the reworded sentence; 11e audits the REAL repository (not a fixture) and finds 1 committed caller, all within arity; 11h still catches all 9 two-argument shapes with shell punctuation and leaves all 12 one-argument shapes unflagged; 11j drives the wrapped-prose class in both directions. GUARDED_PATHS and REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS are byte-identical to aecf003: no scope change, no path added, no exemption touched. No migration, no engine change, no role or privilege change, no personal data, so the CTO migration-approval path is not engaged.
notCompliancePath: None of these three paths is on the R2 list. R2 names services/directus/schema/engine/**, services/directus/schema/migrations/**, tests/db/** and scripts/retention-literal-gate.sh specifically -- not scripts/ as a whole. scripts/dirty-path-guard.sh and scripts/merge-in-gate.sh are on the DIRTY-guard list (all of scripts/) and not on R2, so R2 does not machine-apply to this commit. Asserted by self-test 9e, which fails if the two lists are ever conflated.

afc282Review.whyNotARecordedR2Review: A reviews[] entry would assert that R2's requirement -- a named reviewer who is not the author -- is met. It is not met in the sense that matters: this commit is authored by the CTO (git config user.email = cto@afc.local, verified in the shared tree), and the only reviewer available on this team is the CTO. Per AFC-194 section 5 and the CEO ruling of 2026-10-06, a CTO review of a CTO-team compliance commit is a disclosure, not a second signature, and must not be entered as R2 satisfaction. scripts/dirty-path-guard.sh is not on REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS, so R2 does not machine-apply here; this declaration suppresses no violation and clears no red. The R2 debt stands.
afc282Review.findings: F1 (process, pre-existing): no independent security reviewer seat exists -- the board declined it on cost -- so this is a recorded degradation, not independent review. F2 (design tension, recorded): acceptance criterion 3 asks that a command-position prose sentence not be treated as a caller, while the issue body rejects 'teach the matcher to reject prose' as unsafe. This commit resolves the tension by NOT reading English: it narrows what counts as COMMAND POSITION (bash/sh prefix, column 0, tab recipe) and audits a space-indented bare token only when its argument list carries shell evidence. The residual gap -- a space-indented bare caller with no shell evidence is not pre-flight audited -- is named in the header's NOT-audited list, and the dispatcher remains the boundary that refuses a surplus argument. F3 (residual): the false positive is removed by BOTH the reword and the matcher change; removing either alone would still satisfy criterion 1, so both are asserted (criterion 2 pins the reword, 11j pins the matcher).

The wrapped-prose class is planted in a SEPARATE probe repo by 11j and asserted not-a-caller and not-counted, with two genuine callers still counted; a space-indented bare caller with shell evidence and two arguments is asserted still-caught. 11e audits the real repository: 1 committed caller, within arity. 11h: 12 one-argument shapes unflagged, 9 two-argument shapes caught. 11i: the dispatcher refuses a surplus argument in both modes. No existing assertion changed its verdict; the only new behaviour is the command-position rule and its 11j coverage.
